elements.element: The renewal structure must be either (a) renewal only by mutual written agreement or (b) automatic renewal.
elements.evidence: The clause uses automatic renewal, which is an allowed preferred structure if the remaining automatic-renewal protections are satisfied.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term must be 12 months.
elements.evidence: The clause provides automatic renewal for “an additional one year period” on each anniversary.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer must be able to opt out on 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Either Party, including Customer, may terminate on thirty days' written notice, which permits Customer to prevent the next renewal by specifying the anniversary as the Termination Date.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must provide Customer a reminder 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No operative language requires Vendor to provide any renewal reminder.

elements.element: Any price increase must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no price-increase cap, and the absence of possible price increases elsewhere in the agreement is not demonstrated.
The clause states that the Agreement “shall be automatically renewed” on each anniversary.

elements.element: Customer's required non-renewal notice period must be no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: The redline reduces the notice period to thirty days, and the right is granted to either Party, including Customer.

elements.element: Any price increase must not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: No operative language limits price increases to 5%, and the absence of possible price increases elsewhere is not demonstrated.

result.reason: The redline successfully reduces the notice period to 30 days and retains annual automatic renewals, but it omits both the required 60-day Vendor reminder and any price-increase cap. It therefore reaches neither the preferred nor fallback position. The change is confined to the notice period and does not disturb unrelated terms, although using general termination language rather than express non-renewal language is less precise.
